Qualifications: 10+2 (Science) -> Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT, ~4.5 yrs incl. internship) -> optional Master of Physiotherapy (MPT) in Sports Physiotherapy (2 yrs). State Physiotherapy Council registration where applicable.
Institutes: Jamia Millia Islamia (Delhi) MPT Sports; Sri Ramachandra Institute (Chennai) MPT Sports Physiotherapy; Dr. D.Y. Patil University; Guru Nanak Dev University, Amritsar; Punjabi University, Patiala; Amity Institute of Health Allied Sciences
Notes: India has no single unified statutory physiotherapy licensing body (state/council-level, evolving)
Employers: NSFs, IPL/pro teams, SAI centres, private clinics

Qualifications: Bachelor's/Master's in Nutrition & Dietetics or Food Science + sports-nutrition-specific certificate (NSQF L6 Sports Nutritionist, ACE Fitness Nutrition Specialist, IGMPI Certified Sports Nutritionist)
Institutes: IGMPI Certified Sports Nutritionist; IISDT Diploma in Sports & Fitness Nutrition; NHCA Sports Nutrition & Dietetics Diploma; university M.Sc. Food & Nutrition programmes
Notes: No single unified dietitian licensing law in India
Employers: sports academies, IPL/league teams, fitness chains, hospitals

Qualifications: B.A./B.Sc. Psychology -> M.A./M.Sc. Sport Psychology (2 yrs) + supervised internship
Institutes: LNIPE Gwalior (M.Sc./PG Diploma Sport Psychology); National Sports University, Manipur (M.A. Sports Psychology); Sri Ramachandra Institute, Chennai (M.Sc. Sports & Exercise Psychology); Jain University, Bangalore (PG Diploma); Guru Nanak Dev University, Amritsar
Notes: Clinical practice generally expects RCI registration if offering therapeutic services (not confirmed sport-specific)
Employers: NSFs, SAI, IPL/pro teams

Qualifications: Bachelor's in Sports Science/Physical Education/Exercise Science + international certification, most commonly NSCA-CSCS (Certified Strength & Conditioning Specialist)
Institutes: NSCA Global Chapter India (CSCS exam-prep, ~5 months, ~Rs 60,000 + exam fee); LNIPE Gwalior and NSNIS Patiala for foundational sports science degrees/diplomas
Notes: CSCS is a US-based accreditation, not an Indian statutory license; requires recertification every 3 years
Employers: IPL/league teams, SAI centres, academies

Qualifications: MBBS -> internship -> NEET-PG -> MD in Sports Medicine (3 yrs) OR PG Diploma in Sports Medicine (2 yrs). NMC/State Medical Council registration required.
Institutes: Vardhman Mahavir Medical College & Safdarjung Hospital (Delhi); Armed Forces Medical College (Pune); Sri Ramachandra Medical College (Chennai); NSNIS Patiala PG Diploma (affiliated Baba Farid University of Health Sciences)
Notes: Reported salary Rs 22.9-24 lakh/yr for experienced professionals (source-cited estimate, not independently verified)

Qualifications: Bachelor's in Sports Science/Physiotherapy/Kinesiology -> M.Sc. Sports Biomechanics & Kinesiology (entrance test + physical/medical exam for LNIPE-type institutes)
Institutes: LNIPE Gwalior - Dept. of Sports Biomechanics, M.Sc. Sports Biomechanics; also embedded within MPT Sports Physiotherapy syllabi at various universities
Employers: SAI, NSFs, sports science labs, pro teams

Qualifications: Not standardised in India - common routes: BPT/MPT (rehab-focused), or private certificates (Rehabilitation Fitness Trainer, Fitness Rehabilitation Specialist). US BOC Certification (via NATA-accredited master's) not directly transferable.
Institutes: IISDT - Certificate in Rehabilitation Fitness Trainer / Fitness Rehabilitation Specialist; MPT programmes functioning as the de facto Indian equivalent
Notes: Role often merges with 'Sports Physiotherapist' in Indian job postings

Qualifications: Bachelor's in Exercise Physiology/Physical Education (B.P.Ed/B.Sc.) -> M.Sc. Exercise Physiology
Institutes: LNIPE Gwalior - M.Sc. Exercise Physiology & Nutrition; NSNIS Patiala - Dept. of Exercise Physiology (M.Sc., PG Diploma, certificate courses); SAI Bengaluru (Exercise Physiology division); LNIPE Assam
Employers: SAI centres, NSFs, research institutions

Qualifications: NIS Certificate Course in Sports Coaching (6 weeks) -> Diploma -> 2-yr NIS Master's Diploma (affiliated Punjabi University, Patiala). Federation-specific licenses also apply (e.g. AIFF Grassroots -> C -> B -> A License for football).
Institutes: NSNIS Patiala (principal NIS coaching hub); AIFF coaching license pathway (football); BCCI/NCA pathway for cricket (not independently confirmed - verify directly with NCA/BCCI)
Employers: SAI, state sports departments, NSFs, private academies, schools

Qualifications: Not standardised - no dedicated degree; typically staffed via SAI/NSF coaching cadres or B.P.Ed/M.P.Ed-qualified personnel
Institutes: No dedicated degree identified; key programme is SAI's Khelo India Rising Talent Identification Scheme (KIRTI), which engages coaches, PE teachers and volunteers
Employers: SAI, Khelo India, state sports departments, private academies

Qualifications: General degree (often sports science/management) + specialised video/match-analysis training; practical experience often valued over a fixed degree
Institutes: NSNIS Patiala - PG Diploma in Sports Performance Analysis; CoLLearn Sports Analytics course (NSDC/Skill India); Rajasthan Royals online Sports Analytics certification
Notes: Reported starting salaries up to Rs 8 LPA (source-cited estimate)
Employers: IPL/pro teams, NSFs, analytics companies

Role: Youth Development Officer / Grassroots Development Coach
Qualifications: Discipline-specific grassroots coaching license, e.g. AIFF Grassroots License -> C License (football); role largely federation/club-defined
Institutes: AIFF Grassroots/C/B/A License pathway (football); no single named cross-sport Indian degree programme identified
Employers: football/cricket academies, ISL clubs (e.g. 'Head of Youth Development' roles), state associations

Qualifications: Bachelor's degree (any stream) + typically 5-15 yrs elite sport/coaching/management experience; career path usually via Head Coach/Senior National Coach roles or sports management PG qualifications
Institutes: Feeder qualifications: NSNIS Patiala coaching diplomas, LNIPE degrees, IIM Rohtak Executive PG Diploma in Sports Management, IISWBM PG Diploma in Sports Management
Notes: Verified example: Hockey India 'Director High Performance' role (via SAI jobs portal)

Qualifications: Bachelor's degree (any stream) + Diploma/PG Diploma in Sports Management (1-2 yrs)
Institutes: IIM Rohtak (Executive PG Diploma in Sports Management); IISWBM Kolkata (PG Diploma in Sports Management); NASM Mumbai (UG Diploma in Sports Management)
Employers: private academies, schools/colleges, state/national federations, facility operators

Qualifications: Bachelor's degree (any stream) + PG Diploma/PGDM/PGP in Sports Management (1-2 yrs)
Institutes: ISBR Bangalore (2-yr PGDM Sports Management); IISWBM Kolkata (1-yr PGDSM); IISM Mumbai (11-month PGP/PGDSM); AISTS India (Mumbai, benchmarked to Swiss AISTS standards)
Employers: IPL franchises, BCCI, leagues/federations, event agencies (IMG Reliance, Percept), Khelo India/SAI events. Reported salary: freshers ~Rs 2.5-5 LPA, rising to ~Rs 10 LPA

Qualifications: Sports management diploma/degree common but no single mandatory qualification; sport-specific technical-official pathways run through each NSF (umpiring/refereeing certifications)
Institutes: Not standardised - NSFs (BCCI, AIFF etc.) run own official/technical-delegate tracks; NSNIS Patiala offers officiating-adjacent certificate courses
Notes: Esports tournament management is an emerging, less formalised track
Sources: gaqm.org (international CSM cert, not India-specific), frontlinesmedia.in, productioncrew.in

Qualifications: Diploma/degree in Hotel/Hospitality Management (3-4 yrs, entry after 10+2 ~50%); postgraduate route via MBA in Hospitality Management
Institutes: Institute of Hotel Management (IHM) network under NCHMCT; International Institute of Hotel Management (IIHM); Amity School of Hospitality; admission via NCHMCT JEE/GNIHM JET/LPUNEST
Notes: No dedicated 'sports hospitality' degree in India - filled by hospitality-management graduates moving into sports/event hospitality on the job

Qualifications: Not standardised - typically a graduate with event-management or NGO/community-organising experience; games-specific programmes train coordinators internally
Institutes: No India-specific certification identified; comparable structures at Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games / Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games run in-house training
Notes: Past Indian-hosted events (2010 CWG Delhi) staffed via Organising Committees, university/NSS/NCC partnerships

Qualifications: Degree in business administration/logistics/supply chain, often paired with a sports/event management diploma; hands-on event experience heavily weighted
Institutes: ISST PG Diploma in Sports Management for Working Professionals (covers event logistics for leagues like MPL, Tennis Premier League)
Notes: No dedicated 'sports logistics' certification body in India; role typically absorbed within broader sports/event management qualifications

Qualifications: Bachelor's degree with hospitality/sports management/marketing background; familiarity with CRM, ticketing systems, fan-engagement analytics
Institutes: IISM Mumbai and general BBA/PGDM Sports Management programmes list this as a career outcome rather than a dedicated certificate
Notes: No India-specific 'fan experience' certification found
Employers: IPL franchises, leagues, event companies

Qualifications: Degree/diploma in broadcast engineering or mass communication + 2-4 yrs sports production/broadcasting experience
Institutes: No single dedicated 'sports broadcast operations' course; skills built via general broadcast-engineering/mass-communication diplomas + on-the-job training with broadcasters (Star Sports, Sony Sports Network) or LOCs of ICC/FIFA/AIFF events
Notes: Verified example: AIFF LOC job posting for FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022. India relies more on 'fly-pack' setups than OB vans

Qualifications: PG Diploma/degree in Sports Management covering operations management, event planning, risk assessment, security planning, VIP/hospitality management
Institutes: AISTS India (Mumbai); IISWBM Kolkata (PGDSM); ISST Mumbai; Johan Cruyff Institute's online 'Course in Venue Management and Operations' (international)
Employers: stadium operators, IPL franchises, state sports authorities, venue management companies

Qualifications: Certified Sports Facility Manager (CSFM) certification, or a broader Sports Management degree/PGDM with facility-management modules
Institutes: Sports & Management Research Institute (SMRI) - CSFM course, accredited by Kerala Academy for Skills Excellence (KASE); general BSM/PGDM Sports Management programmes (ISST, IISWBM, IISM)
Notes: SMRI's CSFM appears to be the only India-specific facility-manager-branded certification found

Qualifications: Cricket: BCCI Curator's Certification Course Level 1 (~3 weeks, 75 sessions, 2-day/150-mark exam) covering pitch construction, drainage, soils, grass/weed management. Football/turf generally: no equivalent India-specific body identified.
Institutes: BCCI National Cricket Academy (NCA), Mohali - Curator Certification Course (gold-standard credential for pitch curators); NSNIS Patiala also lists a Ground Management Course
Notes: Course fees reported ~Rs 5,000-10,000

Qualifications: Certificate/Diploma in Gym & Fitness/Fitness Centre Management (~250-450 hours); minimum entry generally 10+2
Institutes: Keleven Fitness Academy (Gym Setup and Management Course, 8 branches); Gayo Fitness Academy (CCFCM, University of Mumbai-approved, NAAC A); ASAP Kerala (Certified General Fitness Trainer, govt. skill scheme); Fit & Met Academy (Diploma in Fitness and Wellness Management)
Notes: Private/skill-development certifications rather than university degrees

Qualifications: Civil/structural engineering degree + project management certification (e.g. PMP); working knowledge of federation facility standards (World Athletics/FIFA/ICC/BWF) and DPR preparation
Institutes: Standard civil engineering degree programmes + PMI's PMP certification (international, widely used in India); specialised short course - Pertecnica Engineering's Stadium & Sports Complex Construction Course for Civil Engineers
Notes: No dedicated Indian university degree titled 'Sports Infrastructure Project Management' found
Employers: SAI, state sports departments (Khelo India), infrastructure contractors

Qualifications: India: private-provider Certificate in Security Officer / Certificate in Cricket & Sports Management (crowd-management, accreditation, risk-assessment modules). International (not India-specific): NCS4's Certified Sport Security Professional (CSSP), UK Level 2/4 Spectator Safety qualifications.
Institutes: Indian Institute of Skill Development Training (IISDT) - Certificate in Security Officer / Diploma in Security Officer Skills and Crisis Management / Certificate in Cricket & Sports Management
Notes: No India-specific equivalent to NCS4's CSSP or UK Spectator Safety found; roles rely on private certificates, in-house training, and international consultancy for large events

Qualifications: Bachelor's/Master's in Product Design or Industrial Design (B.Des/M.Des), or engineering degree (mechanical/product design). No India-specific 'sports goods design' named degree exists.
Institutes: NID Ahmedabad (Industrial Design); IIT Bombay IDC School of Design; IIT Guwahati/Delhi (B.Des Industrial Design); Pearl Academy; MIT Institute of Design Pune; Srishti Manipal Institute
Employers: sporting goods manufacturers/exporters in Jalandhar, Meerut, Delhi-NCR; larger brands' India design studios

Qualifications: B.Tech/B.E. Mechanical, Industrial, or Production Engineering (preferred); MBA in Operations a plus. Employers often weight 3+ yrs floor experience and sector exposure over exact degree.
Institutes: Any AICTE-recognised Mechanical/Production/Industrial Engineering B.Tech; NITIE Mumbai for Industrial Engineering & Operations Management; Punjab Technical University-affiliated colleges (Jalandhar cluster)
Notes: Jalandhar + Meerut account for ~75-80% of India's sports goods production (Jalandhar: 100+ major units, ~20,000 small-scale units)

Qualifications: Bachelor's/Master's in Quality/Industrial/Mechanical Engineering; 2-5 yrs experience common. ASQ's Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) sometimes preferred (international, not India-specific).
Institutes: Any AICTE-recognised Mechanical/Industrial Engineering programme; CIPET (plastics/rubber testing, NABL/BIS-accredited labs); NITRA (textile/apparel QC testing)
Notes: Role involves compliance auditing and BIS/ISO standards testing for exported goods

Qualifications: Bachelor's in Business/Engineering + MBA/specialisation in Supply Chain/Operations Management preferred; 5-8 yrs sourcing/procurement experience often sought
Institutes: MBA with Supply Chain/Operations specialisation (IIMs, NITIE Mumbai, SP Jain, MDI Gurgaon); Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT) for export management
Notes: Sporting Syndicate (Jalandhar, est. 1960) cited as India's largest sports goods manufacturer/exporter and active recruiter

Qualifications: Bachelor's/Master's in Materials Science/Engineering, Polymer/Plastics Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering; 3-6 yrs experience typical for mid-level roles
Institutes: CIPET (R&D centres in Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Bengaluru - polymer/plastics/composites); IIT Materials Science & Metallurgical Engineering departments (Kharagpur, Madras, Bombay, Delhi); NITRA for technical textile R&D
Notes: No India source found describing a dedicated 'sports equipment R&D engineer' job title - role inferred from adjacent materials-science postings; treat as 'varies by employer'

Qualifications: B.Des in Knitwear Design or Textile Design; B.FTech in Apparel Production; short certificate courses in Sportswear Design & Knitting also available
Institutes: NIFT - B.Des Knitwear Design (explicitly covers sportswear/knitted apparel), B.Des Textile Design, B.FTech Apparel Production; NIFT Certificate Programme in Sportswear Design & Knitting
Notes: NIFT's Knitwear Design programme is the most directly sportswear-relevant formal degree found

Qualifications: Bachelor's/Master's from FDDI in Footwear Design & Production, or B.Des in Leather Design (NIFT) with footwear specialisation
Institutes: FDDI (Footwear Design & Development Institute) - Institution of National Importance, 12 campuses (Noida, Chennai, Ankleshwar, Chhindwara, Amethi etc.), curriculum co-designed with IIT Delhi; NIFT B.Des Leather Design; Central Footwear Training Institute (CFTI), Chennai
Notes: FDDI explicitly lists 'Footwear Designer for Fashion and Sport shoes' as a career outcome

Qualifications: Bachelor's/Master's in Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science, or Sports Management; proficiency in R, Python, Tableau, SQL
Institutes: CoLLearn Sports Analytics Course (NSDC/Skill India); Rajasthan Royals Certified Sports Analytics Course (online); Boston Institute of Analytics (Sports Mgmt & Analytics cert/diploma); ISST Pune (industry-led, IPL/ISL practitioners)
Notes: No formal university-degree-level 'sports data analyst' programme yet in India - most credentialing is short certificates on a general STEM/stats degree. Dream Sports and Sportskeeda are active employers

Qualifications: BS/MS Data Science, Statistics, or CS with sports internship experience; OR BS/MS Kinesiology/Exercise Physiology + coding skills. Familiarity with GPS systems (Catapult, STATSports) and video tools (Hudl Sportscode, Dartfish) expected.
Institutes: NSNIS Patiala - Dept. of Sports Biomechanics ('Biomechanics of Human Performance' certificate); NPTEL/SWAYAM free course 'Exercise and Sports Biomechanics'; general data-science degrees + ISST Pune training
Notes: BCCI uses injury/workload tracking for national/U-19 squads; ISL clubs use GPS vests. WPL/Pro Kabaddi cited as expanding this market

Qualifications: B.Tech/B.E. or BCA/MCA in Computer Science, or equivalent software development background; no sports-specific degree exists
Institutes: Any recognised Computer Science engineering programme (IITs, NITs, private colleges); no dedicated 'sports software developer' degree identified
Employers: CricViz (Mumbai ops), Krify, Hyperlink InfoSystem, Spec India, Dream Sports/Dream11

Qualifications: Background in Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field; senior roles need analog/mixed-signal circuits, PCB design, sensor integration, bio-signal processing expertise
Institutes: Biomedical Engineering at IIT Hyderabad, IIT (BHU) Varanasi, IIT Bombay, VIT Vellore; Electrical/Electronics Engineering generally
Notes: India-specific postings for this exact title are sparse; most search results are US-centric. Treat employer/degree matching as 'varies by employer'

Role: Sports Data Scientist / AI in Sports Specialist
Qualifications: Bachelor's in Computer Science/Engineering/Mathematics/Statistics; Master's/PhD in Machine Learning/AI desirable for senior roles
Institutes: IIT Madras - 'Howzzat: Cricstats?' 8-week Cricket Analytics programme (with Pravartak Technologies Foundation & GITAA); IIT Bombay Advanced Certificate Programme in Business Analytics (with Shailesh J. Mehta School of Management)
Notes: Dream Sports has a dedicated sports-domain data science team (ML Scientist, Principal ML Scientist, Director-Data Science roles), working with 250M+ users' data

Qualifications: Engineering background (electronics/CS) for systems/engineering-track roles; sports science/analytics background for on-ground 'Systems Operator' roles. No formal India-specific degree required - trained internally.
Institutes: Not standardised - Hawk-Eye Innovations (part of Sony) recruits both engineering-track and operational staff directly; no specific Indian university partnership identified
Notes: Hawk-Eye covers 30,000+ events across 500+ stadiums in 90+ countries. India-based Cricket Systems Operator roles advertised directly by the company

Qualifications: Bachelor's/Master's in Journalism & Mass Communication (BJMC/MJMC); no dedicated 'sports journalism' degree exists - offered as a specialisation/elective within J&MC
Institutes: Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), New Delhi; Asian College of Journalism, Chennai; Xavier Institute of Communication, Mumbai; Indian Institute of Journalism and New Media, Bangalore
Employers: print/digital sports desks, Sportstar, ESPNcricinfo, news broadcasters

Qualifications: No mandatory degree; typically journalism/mass communication or sports management/sciences background + voice/anchoring training. Broadcast journalism PG diplomas common entry route.
Institutes: IIMC PG Diploma in Radio & TV Journalism; NIMC (New Delhi) Broadcast Journalism; Rajasthan Royals' online Sports Media & Broadcasting course (with Mayanti Langer)
Notes: Deep game knowledge/technical expertise often valued over a formal degree
Employers: Star Sports, JioCinema

Qualifications: Diploma/degree in TV/Radio/Film Production or Mass Communication; 1-yr production diplomas (open to 10+2 pass or graduates) covering pre-production, studio production, editing, vision mixing
Institutes: Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune; Asian Academy of Film and Television (AAFT), Noida; Jamia Millia Islamia AJK Mass Communication Research Centre; Symbiosis Institute of Media and Communication, Pune; IIMC PG Diploma Radio & TV Journalism
Employers: Star Sports, Sony Sports Network, JioCinema, production houses contracted to leagues

Qualifications: Diploma/certificate in Photography and Videography; some institutes offer sports-specific specialisation
Institutes: Symbiosis School of Visual Arts and Photography (SSVAP), Pune; National Institute of Photography; Creative Hut's Professional Diploma in Photography & Cinematography (Sports & Automotive Photography specialisation)
Employers: PTI, ANI, federations, franchises, freelance/agency work

Role: Sports Social Media Manager / Digital Content Creator
Qualifications: No fixed degree path; typically bachelor's in mass communication/marketing + digital/social media certifications (video editing, analytics, platform tools)
Institutes: Meta Blueprint (free); Google Digital Garage; HubSpot Academy; UpGrad/Kraftshala paid programmes; IISDT Diploma in Social Media Marketing and Management
Notes: No sports-specific accredited social-media degree found
Employers: IPL/ISL franchises, federations, sports OTT platforms, athlete-branding agencies

Qualifications: Bachelor's in Communications/Journalism/Public Relations; Master's in PR/Communications or MBA for senior roles
Institutes: IIMC; Xavier Institute of Communication, Mumbai; MICA (Mudra Institute of Communications, Ahmedabad); sports management MBA/PGDM programmes with PR modules
Employers: sports federations, IPL/ISL franchises, PR agencies with sports verticals, athlete management firms

Qualifications: MBA/PGDM in Sports Management or Marketing (2-yr full-time), or bachelor's in sports management/business + specialised certificate
Institutes: SRM Institute of Science and Technology - MBA Sports Management; IIM Ahmedabad Executive Education - Sports & Entertainment Marketing Management Programme; IISM Mumbai - Certificate in Advanced Sports Marketing; TISS Bachelor in Sports Management; IISWBM PG Diploma in Sports Management
Employers: BCCI, JSW Sports, Star Sports, IPL/ISL franchises, GroupM ESP

Qualifications: MBA/PGDM (Marketing/Sales) or Sports Management degree; sales/business-development track record often weighted as much as formal qualification
Institutes: Same sports-management MBA/PGDM ecosystem (SRM, IISM Mumbai, IISWBM, ISBR Bangalore PGDM Sports Management with dual specialisation)
Notes: No dedicated 'sponsorship sales' degree found
Employers: GroupM ESP, Baseline Ventures, franchises, federations

Qualifications: MBA in Marketing/Brand Management or Sports Management
Institutes: Same MBA/PGDM sports management programmes (SRM, ISBR Bangalore, IISM Mumbai, IISWBM); general MBA brand-management specialisations
Employers: Nike India, sportswear/apparel brands, IPL/ISL team brand divisions

Qualifications: No single mandated Indian degree; common backgrounds: Sports Management MBA/PGDM, LLB (contract negotiation), or sports-agent-specific certificate courses
Institutes: Sports Management Worldwide's Sports Agent Advanced Certificate (international); Indian sports-management PGDM/MBA (IISM Mumbai, ISBR Bangalore) with athlete-management modules
Notes: Sports agent is not a licensed profession in India (unlike some Western markets) - flagged by FICCI-commissioned reports as under-regulated
Employers: Baseline Ventures, Cornerstone Sport, independent agents

Qualifications: Bachelor's/MBA in Business/Commerce or Sports Management; operations/finance-oriented role rather than a licensed qualification
Institutes: General sports management MBA/PGDM programmes (SRM, IISM Mumbai, ISBR Bangalore) with venue/revenue-management modules
Notes: No dedicated ticketing-management degree identified in India
Employers: IPL/ISL franchises, stadium/venue operators, BCCI

Qualifications: MBA/PGDM in Marketing, Retail, or Sports Management
Institutes: Same sports-management MBA/PGDM ecosystem (IISM Mumbai, IISWBM, ISBR Bangalore); retail-management specialisations at general B-schools
Notes: Top IPL teams' merchandise revenue reported at Rs 10-20 crore/year (source-cited estimate)

Qualifications: MBA (Operations/General Management) or Sports Management degree; internships with a league/franchise strongly improve placement
Institutes: SRM MBA Sports Management; IISM Mumbai; ISBR Bangalore PGDM Sports Management; TISS Bachelor in Sports Management
Notes: Franchise-level roles span operations, logistics, marketing/sponsorship, ticketing, hospitality, fan engagement
Employers: BCCI/IPL and ISL franchises

Qualifications: Historically no single mandated qualification; under the National Sports Governance Act, 2025 (commenced 31 Dec 2025) and the National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026, President/Secretary General/Treasurer eligibility, election and disqualification criteria are now defined by statute.
Institutes: Sports management PGDM/MBA (IISM Mumbai, IISWBM) combined with governance/administration experience; no specific 'Secretary General' certification course found
Notes: Exact educational qualifications set by each federation's constitution, subject to NSGA 2025 compliance - not a uniform national syllabus

Qualifications: Master's in Public Policy (MPP) or related social science/economics degree; sports-specific specialisation usually built on the job
Institutes: Takshashila Institution's Graduate Certificate/PGP in Public Policy (Bengaluru); IIM Bangalore MPP; Jindal School of Government and Public Policy (O.P. Jindal Global University); TISS; Ashoka University
Notes: Typical track: Research Associate -> Policy Analyst -> Senior Analyst -> Fellow/Director
Employers: think tanks (Takshashila, ORF, CPR, Vidhi Centre), Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, NITI Aayog

Qualifications: LLB (5-yr integrated or 3-yr after graduation); short-term/executive certificate courses in sports law add specialisation
Institutes: Sports Law & Policy Centre (SLPC), Bengaluru (GoSports Foundation + LawNK); Centre for Sports Law and Policy, NUJS Kolkata; Centre for Sports Law and Policy, Symbiosis Law School; NLU Delhi Online Certificate in Sports Law & Safe Sport Practices; MNLU Mumbai Online Certificate (with SAI); NLU Odisha credit course (with Doctrina Ludus)
Employers: federations, franchises, arbitration bodies (Court of Arbitration for Sport matters), law firms with sports practices

Qualifications: Varies by post: Sample Collection Coordinator - graduate degree + 2 yrs relevant experience. Scientific/technical roles (e.g. Senior Scientific Officer) - first-class M.Sc. in Biochemistry/Pharmacology/Chemistry/Sports Science/Medicine + 8 yrs experience, or PhD + 5 yrs.
Institutes: No dedicated Indian degree; built via M.Sc./PhD in Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Chemistry, Sports Science or Medicine + NADA-specific/WADA-recognised training
Notes: NADA India is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports; recruits on deputation/contract/consultant basis

Qualifications: No standardised degree; typically law (LLB), management (MBA), or public administration backgrounds, now shaped by National Sports Governance Act 2025 requirements (ethics compliance, statutory audits, international-charter compliance)
Institutes: Sports law certificate courses (NLU Delhi, MNLU Mumbai, NLU Odisha) + general governance/compliance coursework at law/business schools
Notes: Role newly formalised following NSGA 2025; National Sports Board oversees federation recognition/compliance

Role: Sports Development Officer (Government - SAI/State Sports Dept.)
Qualifications: Generally a graduate/postgraduate degree, often Physical Education or Sports Science; SAI coaching posts often require NIS Diploma in Coaching (NS-NIS Patiala) or equivalent
Institutes: NS-NIS Patiala (SAI) diploma/certificate courses; LNIPE Gwalior (B.P.Ed/M.P.Ed) - commonly used pathway, verify per specific vacancy
Notes: Exact qualification requirements vary by post and are published per recruitment notification - not a single uniform standard
